angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 596,911 km at 372.05 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.6878 +/- 0.0131 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 372.05 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.858 +/- 0.027 solar radii from Ciceri et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-46 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract): 596,911 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.828 +/- 0.076 solar masses from Ciceri et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-46 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5600 K from Ciceri et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-46 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Ciceri et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-46 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-46.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.489, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-46 (pscomppars): spectral type G6 V, from Ciceri et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WASP-46: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-46 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.3 dex, from Ciceri et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-46 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.11113, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-46 (pscomppars): age 9.6 Gyr, from Ciceri et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.456..990C/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-46 (pscomppars): rotation period 16 d, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-46 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.9 km/s, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.858 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.700. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
